newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares slump as new govt hopes dented.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares slump as new govt hopes dented.

text.p: Istanbul shares plunged by more than five percent in late trade on Tuesday after conservative leader Tansu Ciller refused to discuss a planned secularist pact in talks with prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 was 5.24 percent, or 93 points lower at 1,681 at 1247 GMT, about 15 minutes before the close. It was down 3.49 percent at the end of the first session.
"Yesterday's rapid rise turned to selling because of the political developments. Uncertainty over the formation of a new government mounted," said Mustafa Toprak from Es securities.

The index had surged 8.04 percent to a new all-time high close of 1,774 on Monday amid hopes that conservative opposition leader Yilmaz could secure the support of deputies from Ciller's True Path Party.

"I did not discuss the government issue, so as not to legitimise Yilmaz's position," Deputy Prime Minister Ciller told reporters after a 20 minute meeting with Yilmaz, a bitter rival for leadership of the Turkish right.
"We said to Yilmaz 'go immediately and return the mandate to the president'," Ciller said. President Suleyman Demirel on Friday asked Yilmaz to form a government.

Yilmaz is almost assured of the support of two left-wing parties, a right-wing grouping and conservative independents, but he is still around a dozen votes short of the simple majority needed to win a confidence vote in parliament.
